audit.why: Akali owns levels 1-5 and the entry says so. Five Point Strike is energy-gated on a 1.5s cooldown so her poke never stops, while Winter's Wrath is 9s at rank 1 and Arctic Assault 18s. Teamfights swing to Sejuani. The shape is right; the reasons given for it were not.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid all name Akali's level 6 spike as 'Glacial Prison' and describe it as a long-range CC tool.
audit.why: Glacial Prison is Sejuani's own ultimate. Akali's is Perfect Execution: a 675-range two-part dash whose recast executes. The entry therefore tells the reader to fear a long-range stun that does not exist, and hides the one thing that actually kills them — a threshold execute. A player warned about 'her CC' will hold Flash for a stun instead of watching an HP number. spikes[2].text also names Hextech Rocketbelt as her first-item spike; I removed the item name rather than substitute one I cannot verify from the kit files.
audit.corrected: Perfect Execution named with its 675 range and execute recast in whys[4], spikes[1].text and mid; the execute cue now says to track the HP number. spikes[2].text no longer names an item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is never stated: Permafrost is a targeted stun and Twilight Shroud makes Akali unable to be selected by enemy spells. The entry says the Shroud 'dodges' CC and tells the reader to wait until she is 'visible', which describes the wrong mechanic. Frost Armor is also repeatedly called 'your passive Permafrost armor' — six occurrences across whys, wants and prose.
audit.why: Riot's Twilight Shroud text: 'While inside the shroud, Akali becomes invisible and unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks.' Permafrost: 'Sejuani freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks' — a single-target cast at 560 range. So it is not that the stun is likely to miss inside the Shroud; it cannot be cast at all. That turns vague advice into a hard rule with a number: Twilight Shroud is 20s at rank 1 and the whole forward pattern schedules around it. Separately, Permafrost has no passive; the armour and magic resist come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North, and Frost Armor only returns after she is out of combat — which is exactly why her constant chip matters. Attaching it to the wrong ability erases that conditional.
audit.corrected: Twilight Shroud's unselectability stated against Permafrost by name in report[5].t, wants.you[0], early and mid, with the 20s rank-1 cooldown. Frost Armor credited correctly in early and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] and early describe Akali 'stripping your passive Permafrost armor'.
audit.why: Frost Armor is not stripped the way the entry implies — Riot's text says it 'persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage' and returns after she is out of combat. The correct read is that sustained chip keeps her in combat so it never comes back, which is a different instruction: break contact, rather than avoid single autos.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[2] and early now describe keeping Sejuani in combat so Frost Armor never returns.

edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even — Akali takes Q and pokes, you take W and last-hit; neither of you has a real kill threat. At level 2 Shuriken Flip is online at a 16-second cooldown and can punish you for walking up, so track it before stepping into auto range. Your answer arrives at level 3: W twice onto her to fill the Frost gauge, then Permafrost catches her if she has not already popped Twilight Shroud — but if the Shroud is up, stop, because inside it she cannot be selected by your E at all. The game before 6 is about denying her free autos that keep Frost Armor from returning; keep those resistances up and she cannot chunk you.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are where Akali gets comfortable — Twilight Shroud is a 20-second cooldown at rank 1, and while she is inside it she is unselectable by spells, so Permafrost cannot even be cast on her. Freeze near your tower, hold Arctic Assault as an escape rather than an opener, and let her come to you. At level 6 she gets Perfect Execution: a two-part dash whose recast executes, so the number that matters is your HP, not the shape of your bar. Play back far enough that reaching you costs her the first cast, then stun her on the landing. Call for jungle pressure here; Akali inside your CC chain is a free kill.

notes:
'Glacial Prison' is attributed to Akali in three separate fields of this entry. The packet's suspectNames check did not catch it because the name is spelled correctly — it is simply the wrong champion's ultimate. A name-similarity check cannot find this class of error; a check that every named ability belongs to one of the two champions in the matchup would. Worth running across all 71 Sejuani entries, since 'Your Glacial Prison' appears as a suspectName hit in most of them and those are false positives while this one is real.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Glacial Prison can hit Akali inside Twilight Shroud. The Shroud blocks selection by spells and attacks; Glacial Prison stuns 'the first champion hit' as a projectile. Riot's text does not settle whether an unselectable champion is a valid collision target, so I did not state it either way.

Hextech Rocketbelt removed from spikes[2].text as an unverifiable item reference; I did not put another item in its place.
